name: CA-27
label: Likely D

key_factors: Whitesides holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, $2.55 million on hand versus Gibbs's $202,000
The district leans Democratic by six points and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent
Markets give Whitesides about a 95 percent chance of holding the seat

model.rationale: The district's six-point Democratic lean, Whitesides's lopsided cash advantage, and a midterm environment that favors Democrats all point to a comfortable margin; markets price his win odds near 95 percent and no organized outside opposition has emerged on Gibbs's behalf.
model.watch: A shift in the national environment toward Republicans, or late outside spending backing Gibbs, could pull the margin down toward single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Incumbent George T. Whitesides (D) is running.

overview:
Democrats hold this Santa Clarita and Antelope Valley district with George Whitesides, who won the seat in 2024. The district leans Democratic by about six points, and Whitesides enters the campaign with roughly $2.6 million on hand against Jason Gibbs's $202,000, a decisive advertising advantage. No outside groups have spent meaningfully for either side, and no independent general-election polls are available.

Whitesides carried the seat in a year that was difficult for his party, and the midterm environment now tilts toward Democrats, which should widen his margin. Markets give him about a 95 percent chance of holding the seat. With district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money race all pointing the same way, Republicans face long odds, though the absence of polling leaves modest room for surprise.
